plain.li: [spring] The fields are planted. Maybe now someone has time for "{WISH}".
[spring] New season, same request: "{WISH}".
[spring] Everything's growing except "{WISH}".
[spring] I asked for "{WISH}" before the thaw. The thaw's come and gone.
[summer] Long days, plenty of light. Enough for "{WISH}", I'd have thought.
[summer] It's too hot to argue, so I'll just remind you: "{WISH}".
[summer] Half the summer's gone, and "{WISH}" with it, it seems.
[summer] I'd like "{WISH}" before the weather turns, if anyone's counting.
[fall] Before the harvest takes every hand, could someone look at "{WISH}"?
[fall] The leaves are coming down and "{WISH}" still hasn't come up.
[fall] Once the stores are in, "{WISH}" would be a good next thing.
[fall] It's getting colder, and I'm still waiting on "{WISH}".
[clear] Fine weather for getting things done. "{WISH}", for instance.
[clear] Not a cloud in the sky, and no excuse I can see for "{WISH}" waiting.
[clear] Good day for it, if anyone's looking for a job: "{WISH}".
[clear] Clear skies all week. I've been looking at the spot where "{WISH}" would go.
[highmood] I'm in a good mood, so I'll ask nicely: "{WISH}"?
[highmood] Things are going well. "{WISH}" would make them go better.
[highmood] Good week. I'd like it to end with "{WISH}".
[trusting] I'm not worried. I just don't want "{WISH}" to slip through the cracks.
[trusting] You've never let me down before, so I'm only checking on "{WISH}".
[night] Up late again, and "{WISH}" is the first thing I thought of.

warm.li: When there's a moment to spare, I'm still thinking about "{WISH}". Only when there's a moment.
I don't want to add to anyone's load. I'd just love "{WISH}", someday soon.
Thank you for listening the first time. I'm still hoping, that's all.
I'd offer to help with "{WISH}" myself, if someone tells me what to fetch.
No pressure. "{WISH}" would just make my days a little easier.

blunt.li: How long does "{WISH}" take? Longer than this?
I asked. You heard. Now do it.
Still no "{WISH}". I'll keep saying it.

cheerful.li: Guess what I'm still dreaming about? "{WISH}"!
Friendly reminder number three: "{WISH}". I'm keeping count, kindly.
I've already picked a spot for "{WISH}" and a name for it.
Still hoping, still smiling, still asking about "{WISH}".
Don't mind me, I'm only waving the "{WISH}" flag again.

gloomy.li: "{WISH}". I keep mentioning it, the way you keep pressing a bruise.
I suppose "{WISH}" is waiting behind a dozen other things.
Another day without "{WISH}". They add up.
I'm still waiting. I don't expect much, but I'm still waiting.
Maybe "{WISH}" will happen. Maybe I'll stop asking first.

cold.li: "{WISH}" is overdue. I'll be raising it at the next meeting.
I've waited a reasonable time for "{WISH}". We are now past it.
A request left open this long starts to look like a refusal.
"{WISH}". I'd like a date, or a reason.
My patience on "{WISH}" has a limit, and we're approaching it.

plain.li: [spring] {PAWN_nameDef} picks a flower on the way over and leaves it there, as thanks.
[spring] It's the first warm day of the year, and {PAWN_nameDef} spends a good part of it just looking.
[spring] {PAWN_nameDef} comes in muddy from the fields, sees it, and forgets to take {PAWN_possessive} boots off.
[summer] {PAWN_nameDef} sits beside it in the long evening light until the insects drive {PAWN_objective} in.
[summer] Despite the heat, {PAWN_nameDef} walks over twice before supper to look at it again.
[fall] {PAWN_nameDef} sets down an armful of harvest to take a proper look.
[fall] With the wind getting colder, {PAWN_nameDef} says it came at just the right time.
[fall] {PAWN_nameDef} shows it to everyone coming in from the fields, one by one.
[winter] {PAWN_nameDef} blows on {PAWN_possessive} hands, grins at it, and says it was worth the wait.
[winter] In the dull light of a winter afternoon, it's the brightest thing {PAWN_nameDef} has seen in weeks.
[clear] {PAWN_nameDef} stands with it in the sun for a while, saying nothing, looking pleased.
[clear] On a clear, still day, {PAWN_nameDef} takes everyone over to see it.
[clear] {PAWN_nameDef} spends the fine afternoon finding excuses to walk past it.
[highmood] {PAWN_nameDef} was in a good mood already. Now nobody can get a word in.
[highmood] {PAWN_nameDef} thanks the council, then the builders, then the cook, who had nothing to do with it.
[highmood] {PAWN_nameDef} whistles all the way back to work.
I was going to ask for the same thing. {OTHER_nameDef} beat me to it.
"{WISH}" would help me too. Put me down.
I'm adding my voice to {OTHER_nameDef}'s. Two is harder to ignore.
{OTHER_nameDef} isn't the only one who's been thinking about "{WISH}".
Whatever {OTHER_nameDef} is getting, I'd like the same written down for me.
I've been meaning to ask for this since the first week. {OTHER_nameDef} just said it first.
I'll ask alongside {OTHER_nameDef}. We'll share the work if it helps.

warm.li: If it helps {OTHER_nameDef}'s case, I'm asking too.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked nicely, so I'll ask nicely as well.
I want it for {OTHER_nameDef} as much as for me.
Put my name next to {OTHER_nameDef}'s, and thank you for listening to both of us.

blunt.li: Same as {OTHER_nameDef}. Two of us now.
Me as well. Don't make us ask twice.
"{WISH}". Two votes. Get on with it.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I are a team now! Team "{WISH}".
I'll ask too, and if that's not enough, I'll ask again tomorrow!
What a good idea {OTHER_nameDef} had. I'm stealing half of it.
Two of us! That's practically a crowd.

gloomy.li: I'll put my name down too. Maybe two names count for more than one.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked, so I'm asking. I don't expect it to matter.
Same request as {OTHER_nameDef}. Same chance of it happening, I'd guess.
Count me in, for what it's worth.

cold.li: I'm co-signing. It's more efficient than asking separately.
{OTHER_nameDef}'s request benefits me. I'll support it.
Two requests for "{WISH}" make it a priority, by any fair measure.
Add my name. I'll be watching how long it takes.

plain.li: [spring] {PAWN_nameDef} pointed out that it was planting season, and asked whether "{AMBITION}" could be eaten.
[spring] {PAWN_nameDef} asked whether "{AMBITION}" would still matter once the fields needed every hand.
[spring] {PAWN_nameDef} said every spring brings a big idea, and every summer buries it.
[summer] {PAWN_nameDef} fanned {PAWN_objective}self through {OTHER_nameDef}'s pitch and asked who'd haul stone in this heat.
[summer] {PAWN_nameDef} said "{AMBITION}" sounded lovely, and asked whether it came with shade.
[summer] {PAWN_nameDef} asked {OTHER_nameDef} to finish quickly, since the evening was the only cool part of the day.
[fall] {PAWN_nameDef} wanted to know whether "{AMBITION}" came before or after the harvest, because it couldn't be both.
[fall] {PAWN_nameDef} asked how "{AMBITION}" would keep anyone warm this winter.
[fall] {PAWN_nameDef} said the colony had a harvest to bring in, and that was ambition enough.
[winter] {PAWN_nameDef} asked whether "{AMBITION}" could be built in the snow, and by whom.
[winter] {PAWN_nameDef} said {PAWN_pronoun} would vote for anything that came with firewood.
[night] {PAWN_nameDef} asked whether this could be settled in the morning, then stayed to argue anyway.
[night] {PAWN_nameDef} pointed out the hour, and that "{AMBITION}" had already taken most of it.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} said {PAWN_pronoun} liked the idea and only worried about who would do the work.
{PAWN_nameDef} asked {OTHER_nameDef} to slow down so the newer ones could follow.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} said "{AMBITION}" was the third grand plan this year, and asked what happened to the other two.
{PAWN_nameDef} said "no" before the pitch was over, then sat back.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} asked whether "{AMBITION}" could have a party at the end of it, and seemed to mean it.
{PAWN_nameDef} shouted a suggestion halfway through the pitch, and it was a good one.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} said {PAWN_pronoun} had heard pitches like this before, at the last place, before it burned.
{PAWN_nameDef} listened to all of it and said it sounded like a lot of work for people who were already tired.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} asked {OTHER_nameDef} what "{AMBITION}" would cost, then asked again when the answer was vague.
{PAWN_nameDef} wanted to know who would answer for it if "{AMBITION}" failed halfway.

plain.li: [spring] It's spring. If we start "{AMBITION}" now, we'll see it done before the cold.
[spring] Fresh season, fresh start. "{AMBITION}" has my vote.
[spring] The ground's soft and the days are long. Good time for "{AMBITION}".
[summer] We've got the light and the hands. Let's do "{AMBITION}".
[summer] Summer's the time for big work. I'm for it.
[summer] Better to sweat over "{AMBITION}" now than freeze over it later.
[fall] If we're doing "{AMBITION}", let's get it done before the snow.
[fall] The harvest's nearly in. After that, I'm all for "{AMBITION}".
[fall] We'll want "{AMBITION}" before winter. I'm voting yes.
[winter] We're stuck indoors anyway. Might as well plan "{AMBITION}" properly.
[winter] Something to work toward will get us through the cold. "{AMBITION}", then.
[night] It's late and I'm tired, and I still think {OTHER_nameDef} is right.
[night] Let's vote and go to bed. I'm for it.
[night] I'll keep it short, since it's late: yes to "{AMBITION}".
[clear] It's been a fine week. Let's use the good weather for "{AMBITION}".
[clear] The weather's with us. So am I.
[clear] Clear skies, good tempers. Best time to start something.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has worked hard on this. The least I can do is vote for it.
It would mean a lot to some of us. I'm for it.

blunt.li: I'm for it. Let's not talk it to death.

cheerful.li: Yes, yes, a hundred times yes to "{AMBITION}"!
I've been waiting for someone to suggest this. Put me down for the first shift.

gloomy.li: It's the least bad idea I've heard all season. I'll vote for it.
We'll probably regret something this year. Let it not be skipping "{AMBITION}".

cold.li: The numbers on "{AMBITION}" work. I'm in favor.
It's the sensible choice. I'll support {OTHER_nameDef} on it.

plain.li: [spring] It's planting season. Where are the hands for "{AMBITION}" coming from?
[spring] Let's get the fields in first. "{AMBITION}" will keep.
[spring] Spring makes everyone ambitious. Summer makes them tired.
[summer] In this heat? I'd like to see {OTHER_nameDef} haul the first load.
[summer] Half of us are already worn out from the fields.
[fall] The harvest isn't in yet. Can this wait?
[fall] We need to be thinking about winter, not "{AMBITION}".
[fall] Every hand on "{AMBITION}" is a hand not bringing in the crops.
[winter] With what light? The days are four hours long.
[night] It's late. Let's not decide something this big half asleep.
[night] Can we talk about this when we're all awake?
[night] I'm too tired to vote for anything this big.

warm.li: I'd love to say yes. I'm just not sure we have it in us right now.
Could we try something smaller first, and work up to it?

cheerful.li: It's a lovely idea! I just think we'll need about twice as many of us.
I'm not saying no! I'm saying not yet, with a smile.

gloomy.li: We'll start it, and we won't finish it, and we'll feel worse than if we'd never tried.
Big plans tend to end with someone hurt.

cold.li: The cost of "{AMBITION}" outweighs what it brings. I'm against it.
I'd like {OTHER_nameDef} to show the work before I vote for it.

plain.li: [spring] Somebody's tracked half the field in on their boots.
[spring] Can we keep this short? The seedlings need watering.
[spring] I can smell the rain coming. Let's be quick.
[summer] Whoever's sitting by the door, prop it open.
[summer] It's too hot to think. Let me know how I voted.
[summer] Is there any water left in that jug?
[fall] I've still got baskets to carry before dark.
[fall] Who brought apples? Can I have one?
[fall] The wind's picking up. Somebody check the shutters after this.
[winter] Pass the blanket. No, the other one.
[winter] Has anyone seen my other glove?
[winter] Sit closer to the fire, it's free.
[night] I'm going to be useless tomorrow.

warm.li: Shift up, there's room for one more on the bench.
Who's minding the children? Oh, good.

cheerful.li: I brought snacks! Well, one snack. Who wants to share?

gloomy.li: I'll forget all of this by tomorrow.

cold.li: I've counted four people who haven't said a word.

plain.li: Last time I'll mention "{WISH}". I mean it this time.
There's not long left. "{WISH}", or I let it go.
I'd like an answer on "{WISH}" before the time runs out, even if it's no.
I'm asking one last time. After this, I'll know where I stand.
If "{WISH}" isn't coming, someone tell me so I can stop waiting.
Days left, not weeks. "{WISH}".

warm.li: I know it's late to ask again. "{WISH}" still matters to me.
I won't be angry if it can't be done. I'd just like to know.
One last nudge, and then I'll leave it in your hands.
If there's any way, I'd still be grateful for "{WISH}". Truly.
I've tried to be patient. I'm still trying.
Please, before the time's up. That's all.

blunt.li: Time's nearly out. So's my patience.

cheerful.li: Last call for "{WISH}"! Final offer, while stocks last.
It's the eleventh hour! Still a whole hour, though.
One more try for "{WISH}". I believe in miracles, mostly.
Nearly out of time! Good thing I'm stubborn.
Last reminder about "{WISH}", I promise. Almost certainly.
Still hoping, right up to the end!

gloomy.li: Time's nearly up on "{WISH}". So is the hope.
I'll ask once more, so I can't say I didn't.
It's going to lapse, isn't it.
Last chance for "{WISH}". I already know how this ends.
I've stopped expecting it. I'm only asking out of habit.
Nearly over. I'll start forgetting it now.

cold.li: Final notice on "{WISH}". Silence will be taken as no.
"{WISH}" expires soon. I'll draw my own conclusions.
This is the last time I raise it. Remember that I did.
The window for "{WISH}" is closing. So is mine.
I've given the council every chance. This is the last one.
If "{WISH}" lapses, I'll treat it as a choice, not an accident.

plain.li: "{WISH}" is fine, {OTHER_nameDef}, but it can't come before the roof.
I'm not against "{WISH}". I'm against it this week.
We've three other jobs half done. "{WISH}" would make four.

warm.li: I'd like {OTHER_nameDef} to have it, truly. Just not before the ones going without.
Let's come back to "{WISH}" when things are calmer, {OTHER_nameDef}. I'll speak for it then.

blunt.li: Not now. We've got bigger problems.

cheerful.li: Oh, it's a nice idea! Can we have it after we've stopped being hungry?
I love it, {OTHER_nameDef}, and I'll love it even more next season.

gloomy.li: We can't afford it. We can't afford most things.
The moment we start "{WISH}", something else will fall apart.

cold.li: "{WISH}" is a luxury. We aren't in a position for luxuries.
I'd want to see what it costs before anyone says yes, {OTHER_nameDef}.

plain.li: No. Right. I'll find some other way.
I'd hoped for a yes. I'll take the no and go.
[trusting] You've been fair with me before, so I'll trust this one.
[trusting] If it's no, there's a reason. I'll ask what it is, later.

warm.li: I understand. Maybe another time.

cheerful.li: Ah well! Can't win them all, and I've got plenty of other wishes.

gloomy.li: No. Of course.

cold.li: Refused. I'll adjust my expectations of the council.

plain.li: [spring] {PAWN_nameDef} comes in from the planting, dirt to the elbows, and says there's something {PAWN_pronoun} wants.
[summer] In the slow heat of the afternoon, {PAWN_nameDef} finds a shady spot and a listener.
[summer] {PAWN_nameDef} waits until the worst of the heat has passed, then brings it up.
[summer] Sitting out on a long summer evening, {PAWN_nameDef} decides it's time to ask.
[fall] {PAWN_nameDef} sets down a basket of the harvest and says it plainly.
[fall] With the first cold winds coming through, {PAWN_nameDef} has a request before winter.
[winter] Huddled by the fire, {PAWN_nameDef} raises something that's been on {PAWN_possessive} mind for weeks.
[winter] Snowbound and restless, {PAWN_nameDef} finally asks.
[winter] {PAWN_nameDef} knocks the frost off {PAWN_possessive} collar and gets to the point.
[clear] On a fine clear day, {PAWN_nameDef} catches someone between jobs.
[clear] {PAWN_nameDef} sits on the step in the sun and calls someone over to hear it.
[clear] It's a good day, and {PAWN_nameDef} decides a good day is the time to ask.
[trusting] {PAWN_nameDef} asks easily, as if the answer is already yes.
[highmood] {PAWN_nameDef} is grinning when {PAWN_pronoun} asks, which is hard to say no to.
[lowmood] {PAWN_nameDef} asks quietly, without looking up.
Only a few days left for "{AMBITION}". Every pair of hands counts now.
I've counted what's left to do on "{AMBITION}". It's a lot, and the days are few.
If anyone can spare an hour, "{AMBITION}" needs it.
[night] Up late going over "{AMBITION}" again. We're so close and so short.
[night] I lay awake doing the sums on "{AMBITION}". They don't come out well.

warm.li: Whatever happens with "{AMBITION}", thank you for trying so hard.
We're tired, I know. A little more, together.

cheerful.li: Down to the wire on "{AMBITION}"! This is the exciting part.
Nearly there! Well, nearly nearly.

gloomy.li: We're going to miss it. I can feel it.
I keep looking at what's left of "{AMBITION}" and feeling sick.

cold.li: The deadline on "{AMBITION}" is close. I want everyone not on essential work on it.
Failure on "{AMBITION}" will cost us more than the effort to finish it.

plain.li: Half of "{AMBITION}" done. I didn't think we'd get this far this fast.
We're halfway. The second half's always slower, so let's not stop.
[winter] Halfway, and the cold hasn't stopped us yet.
[winter] Half done, with frost on every tool. Not bad.
[afterraid] Even with the raid, we're halfway. That says something about us.
[afterraid] We lost days to the fighting and still kept going. Halfway.

warm.li: Halfway, and everyone's done their share. I'm proud of us.
Half done. Let's make sure nobody's carrying more than their part.

blunt.li: Halfway. No time to admire it.

cheerful.li: Halfway! I'm going to celebrate by working twice as hard. Or by having a nap.
Half of "{AMBITION}"! The second half will be easier, because I've decided it will.

gloomy.li: Halfway. The easy half, if past jobs are anything to go by.
Half done. I'll believe in the rest when I see it.

cold.li: Fifty percent. On schedule, give or take a day.
Halfway. The pace is acceptable. I'd like it better.

plain.li: Word has come: {X_nameDef}, who {DEED}, is dead.
{X_nameDef} is dead. {VICTIM} won't have to watch the horizon for {X_nameDef} anymore.
The news reached the colony today. {X_nameDef}, who {DEED}, will not be back.
{X_nameDef} is gone for good. What {X_nameDef} did to {VICTIM} stays, but {X_nameDef} doesn't.
[person,loose] A traveler passing through mentioned {X_nameDef}'s death as if it were weather. {VICTIM} asked them to say it again.
[person,loose] {X_nameDef}, who {DEED}, died far from here, of something nobody bothered to name.
[person,captive] {X_nameDef} died in the cells. {VICTIM} went to look, once, and then went back to work.
[person,captive] {X_nameDef}, who {DEED}, will be buried by the people {X_nameDef} hurt.
[beast,loose] What was left of the beast that {DEED} turned up in the brush, picked clean.
[beast,captive] The beast that {DEED} died in its pen. {VICTIM} stood at the rail for a long time afterward.

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} is dead. It doesn't undo anything.

cold.li: {X_nameDef}, who {DEED}, is dead. One less thing to plan around.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is gone, and so the oath against {FACTION} for {LOST} passes to {PAWN_nameDef}.
{PAWN_nameDef} kept {OTHER_nameDef}'s promise: {FACTION} still owe for {LOST}, and {PAWN_nameDef} means to collect.
{PAWN_nameDef} said it at the graveside, so everyone heard: the account with {FACTION} for {LOST} stays open.
{OTHER_nameDef}'s vendetta against {FACTION} didn't die with {OTHER_objective}. {PAWN_nameDef} carries it now, for {LOST}.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has taken up {OTHER_nameDef}'s oath against {FACTION}, for {LOST} and for {OTHER_nameDef}.
{PAWN_nameDef} promised {OTHER_nameDef}'s memory that {FACTION} would answer for {LOST}.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died owed. {PAWN_nameDef} will take payment from {FACTION} for {LOST}.
{PAWN_nameDef} picked up the vendetta where {OTHER_nameDef} dropped it. {FACTION}, {LOST}. Simple.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has sworn to finish {OTHER_nameDef}'s quarrel with {FACTION} over {LOST}, and says {OTHER_nameDef} would have laughed to see it.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} took on {OTHER_nameDef}'s oath against {FACTION} for {LOST}, knowing where oaths like that lead.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has taken over {OTHER_nameDef}'s claim on {FACTION} for {LOST}. Debts like that don't lapse.
